title: Lesson 3｜Gender Stereotypes About Jobs
sentences: Picture this: / a badly hurt woman / is taken to a hospital.
想像一下：一位受重傷的女性被送到醫院。
A doctor and a nurse / are treating her.
一位醫生和一位護理師正在為她治療。
You are thinking of the doctor / as a man, / aren’t you?
你正在把醫生想像成男性，對吧？
If so, / it’s possible / that you might have a gender stereotype.
如果是這樣，你很可能有性別刻板印象。
Since we were little, / we have been taught / “There are jobs for women and jobs for men.”
從我們小時候起，我們就被教導：「有些工作適合女性，有些工作適合男性。」
Gender stereotypes about jobs / are formed in childhood.
職業的性別刻板印象在童年時期形成。
We learn these stereotypes / from our parents, relatives, or the media.
我們從父母、親戚或媒體學到這些刻板印象。
Men are often expected / to do public service jobs, / such as doctors or policemen.
人們通常期待男性從事公共服務工作，例如醫生或警察。
On the other hand, / women are thought to be better / at caring and teaching jobs, / such as nurses or teachers.
另一方面，人們認為女性比較擅長照護和教學工作，例如護理師或教師。
As you can see, / gender stereotypes about jobs / are everywhere.
如你所見，職業的性別刻板印象無所不在。
One toy company, Mattel, / is trying to break / gender stereotypes.
一家玩具公司美泰兒正試圖打破性別刻板印象。
It has helped a lot / to make the job market more equal / over the years.
多年來，它對促進職場平等有很大的幫助。
Its Barbie doll / is known as / one of the most hard-working toys / in the world.
它的芭比娃娃被認為是世界上最勤奮的玩具之一。
Since 1959, / Barbie has had over 250 jobs, / such as a doctor, a lawyer, an engineer, a singer, / and even the president of the United States!
自 1959 年以來，芭比從事過超過 250 種職業，例如醫生、律師、工程師、歌手，甚至美國總統！

title: Lesson 3 DIalogue
sentences: Nick: Hey, Mindy, / look at these book covers.
嘿，Mindy，看看這些書的封面。
Nick: Why is the Boys’ Life one / filled with airplanes, computers, and robots?
為什麼這本《男孩的生活》充滿飛機、電腦和機器人？
Mindy: Right, / and the Girls’ Life one / shouldn’t be only about fashion and hair styles, / should it?
對啊，而這本《女孩的生活》不該只是關於時尚和髮型，對吧？
Nick: Yes, / I think it’s stupid.
對，我認為那很愚蠢。
Nick: To be honest, / my sister loves robots, cars, and science toys.
老實說，我姊姊喜歡機器人、汽車和科學玩具。
Nick: Why should those / only be for boys?
為什麼那些玩具只該給男孩玩？
Mindy: I know!
我懂！
Mindy: I wanted a Spider-Man comic book / when I was little, / but my cousin said, / “That’s not for girls.”
我小時候想要一本蜘蛛人漫畫書，但是我表哥說：「那不是給女生的。」
Mindy: It made me so mad!
那讓我好生氣！
Nick: I totally understand.
我完全可以理解。
Nick: I hoped to buy a toy cooking set once, / but I didn’t.
我曾經希望買一組玩具廚具，但我沒那麼做。
Nick: I was afraid / I would be laughed at by others.
我害怕我會被其他人嘲笑。
Mindy: That’s not right.
那是不對的。
Mindy: Everyone should be allowed / to choose their own toys.
每個人都應該被允許選擇自己的玩具。
Mindy: Toys don’t have a gender, / do they?
玩具沒有性別，對嗎？
Nick: Good point.
說得好。
Nick: If Barbie can be a doctor, a lawyer, or an engineer, / then all kids should be free / to play with all kinds of toys.
如果芭比娃娃可以當醫生、律師或工程師，那麼所有孩子都應該能自由地玩各種玩具。
Mindy: Yeah, / I heard some parents in the UK / started a group Let Toys Be Toys.
對呀，我聽說在英國有些家長成立了一個團體「讓玩具就是玩具」。
Mindy: It asked stores / to stop using words like / “toys for boys” or “toys for girls.”
它要求商店停止使用像是「給男孩的玩具」或「給女孩的玩具」這樣的字眼。
Nick: That’s a good idea!
那是個很棒的點子！
Nick: It’s time / to break these toy “rules,” / isn’t it?
是時候打破這些玩具的「規則」了，不是嗎？
